correctness.rationale: Equation (1) in RESULT.md follows from direct rank-one factorization. Fixing phi(x0)=1 forces phi(xa)=c phi(x), and applying phi to xa^2 via a^2=2ca gives c^2=2c^2, hence c=0 over every field. Thus a^2=0 and phi(aA)=0 are necessary and sufficient. In k[t]/t^n this means 2 v(a)>=n and phi annihilates exactly the ideal t^{v(a)}A. The rank-one determinantal cones, intersections and dimensions follow from explicit W_i,U_i dimensions. Nonzero rank-one cones are smooth; intersections are precisely the singular support of the reduced union. The projective degree adds because all components have dimension n-2 and lower-dimensional intersections. Scalar-equivalence of (a,phi) gives exactly q^(n-i-1)(q^i-1) points per valuation. Standalone CHECKER.py directly tested all basis Rota-Baxter equations on 77267 normalized nonzero rank-one maps across 13 finite cases including GF(4); finite cases are corroborative, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Full primary-text comparisons identify Guo–Rosenkranz–Zheng (2014) and Yu (2015) as studies of monomial and injective operators on the untruncated polynomial ring; Farooq (2026) treats the square-zero-radical algebra K[x_1,...,x_r]/m^2 rather than k[t]/t^n for n>=4. A previously known length-three truncation case is explicitly excluded. The claim is the complete reduced rank-one locus, h equidimensional components, exact intersections and singular locus, and all-prime-power point counts over all n>=4. No located result has the same or stronger implications. Elementary universal rank-one and Segre lemmas are tools, not claimed new. Absolute publication priority is uncertain.

value.rationale: Rank-one maps form the first nonzero determinantal stratum of a natural operator variety for integral-like algebraic structures. For every truncation n>=4 and every field the result identifies h=floor(n/2) distinct Segre-cone components of equal dimension, their exact pairwise intersections and codimension-one singular locus; this explains how nilpotency length induces reducible geometry rather than just counting a tiny example. The finite-field polynomial provides exact size and valuation-resolved frequencies in every characteristic, relevant for understanding the prevalence of low-rank integration-type operations. The phenomenon does not follow from the known n=2 and n=3 boundary classifications or from generic Segre facts without the Rota–Baxter/ideal-filtration reduction.
